GENERAL SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM #4
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Overgrazing continuously

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cell division? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cell division.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cell division.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Cell division.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cell division.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Ecosystems? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Ecosystems.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on The Ecosystems.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Ecosystems.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Ecosystems.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters.? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Genetics ● Meaning of terms and concepts in genetics (Deoxyribon? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Genetics ● Meaning of terms and concepts in genetics (Deoxyribon.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Genetics ● Meaning of terms and concepts in genetics (Deoxyribon.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Genetics ● Meaning of terms and concepts in genetics (Deoxyribon.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Genetics ● Meaning of terms and concepts in genetics (Deoxyribon.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrostatics? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrostatics.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrostatics.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Electrostatics.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrostatics.

8. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

9. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Glucose and oxygen

10. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Producers

11. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Milk souring

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Polymers? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Polymers.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Polymers.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Polymers.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Polymers.

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrolysis? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrolysis.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrolysis.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrolysis.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Electrolysis.

14. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Carbon and its Oxides? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Carbon and its Oxides.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Carbon and its Oxides.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Carbon and its Oxides.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Carbon and its Oxides.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Evolution and Biodiversity? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Evolution and Biodiversity.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Evolution and Biodiversity.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Evolution and Biodiversity.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Evolution and Biodiversity.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Cell division and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Genetics ● Meaning of terms and concepts in genetics (Deoxyribon and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Evolution and Biodiversity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Skeletal and Muscular System and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Carbon and its Oxides and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters. and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
